parameters.excerpt: The current standard only supports PMLEN=XLEN-48 (i.e., PMLEN=16 in RV64) and PMLEN=XLEN-57 (i.e., PMLEN=7 in RV64). A setting has been reserved to potentially support other values of PMLEN in future standards.
parameters.reasoning: PMLEN is a direct implementation parameter that determines how many upper bits are masked. The spec defines specific supported values (16 or 7 for RV64) that implementations must choose from.

parameters.excerpt: Pointer masking only applies to RV64. In RV32, trying to enable pointer masking will result in an illegal WARL write and not update the pointer masking configuration bits
parameters.reasoning: This is a direct implementation choice about whether pointer masking is supported in RV32. The spec states it only applies to RV64, making this a binary architectural parameter.

parameters.excerpt: Profiles and implementations may choose to support an arbitrary subset of these extensions and must define valid ranges for their corresponding values of PMLEN.
parameters.reasoning: Implementations can choose which subset of pointer masking extensions (Ssnpm, Smnpm, Smmpm, etc.) to support. This is a direct implementation choice of selecting from a defined set.
